subject: Procurement pathway for fintech POC: marketplace first or direct enterprise?
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acme-fintech.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-fintech.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Options for procurement — AWS Marketplace vs direct contract for POC

Hi Jonas,

We're evaluating Redwood for a time-boxed POC (3–4 weeks) that will run in our US region and will touch customer transaction metadata (no raw PII). Procurement has asked me to confirm whether we should go through our cloud marketplace (AWS) or pursue a direct enterprise contract with Redwood. A few constraints that matter for us:

- We need the vendor to demonstrate SOC 2 evidence and support data residency controls during the POC.
- Our finance team prefers marketplace purchases when possible because it reduces procurement lead time, but the legal team says marketplace purchases sometimes limit custom SLAs and invoice/ tax handling.
- We may want a follow-on enterprise contract if POC is successful; curious how a marketplace start impacts that path.

Can you summarize tradeoffs and recommend a path that minimizes time-to-POC but keeps the option for enterprise terms later? Also, any checklist or docs you can share would be helpful.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Cole
Head of Infrastructure & Procurement
ACME Fintech

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acme-fintech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Options for procurement — AWS Marketplace vs direct contract for POC

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: start on the AWS Marketplace for a fast POC, while we run enterprise contracting in parallel if you think you’ll move to a committed deployment. Below is a concise tradeoff summary and a recommended stepwise approach.

Tradeoffs (high level)
- Marketplace (pros): fastest procurement path (often days), simplified invoicing through AWS, good for transactable POCs, can leverage co-sell programs to get AWS introductions.
- Marketplace (cons): limited ability to negotiate MSA-level custom terms, some regulatory controls (e.g., data residency, egress terms) are harder to negotiate via standard marketplace flow unless you use a Private Offer / Contracting via Seller Private Offers.
- Direct contract (pros): full flexibility on SLAs, custom security addenda, indemnities, and preferred commercial terms. Better for long-term commitments and committed capacity (Dedicated).
- Direct contract (cons): longer procurement cycle (often 4–8+ weeks), requires finance + legal review.

Recommended path for ACME Fintech (given your constraints)
1) Marketplace Private Offer for the POC: list the POC as a private offer (transactable) on AWS Marketplace. This gets procurement and finance comfortable with the marketplace billing model and accelerates_startup. We can attach a Seller Private Offer that includes explicit data residency notes and a short acceptance of our SOC2 controls.
2) Parallel legal track: our contracts team will open a parallel negotiation for an MSA with enterprise terms. The private offer can be time-boxed and explicitly converted into an enterprise agreement later; we commonly credit marketplace spend toward the first invoice on a direct contract.
3) Co-sell / AWS engagement: if you want AWS to assist (co-sell), we’ll need to submit the opportunity to AWS via their Partner Central. That can help with introductions but adds a bit of alignment work (partner owner, contact, and deal registration).

I’m attaching a short AWS marketplace checklist and a draft MSA to illustrate what we can negotiate.

Next steps
- If this sounds good, let’s schedule a 30-minute sync today or tomorrow to confirm the Private Offer SKUs and any required contract clauses (data residency / egress / SOC2 evidence).
- I’ll loop in our legal (Marcus) and sales ops (Laura) on the call.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Options for procurement — AWS Marketplace vs direct contract for POC

Thanks Jonas — that direction sounds very sensible. A couple of quick clarifications before we sync:

1) Pricing / credits: if we buy via a Marketplace private offer for the POC and then sign a direct enterprise contract, can Redwood credit the Marketplace spend toward the enterprise commitment? Our CFO wants clear confirmation of that.

2) Marketplace surcharge: does the Marketplace add a fee on top of the list price? Who is invoiced (ACME via AWS vs Redwood invoicing us directly) and how do taxes get handled?

3) Timeline: procurement wants the shortest possible time-to-POC. If we proceed with a Private Offer, can we realistically be live in 3–5 business days?

I’ll book the 30-minute slot once I see a couple of proposed times.

Regards,
Samantha

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Options for procurement — AWS Marketplace vs direct contract for POC

Hi Samantha — quick answers to your questions below.

1) Marketplace crediting: Yes — we commonly credit Marketplace spend toward the first invoice on a direct contract. The standard approach is to document the credit in the MSA or an addendum (we can add a clause that nets the marketplace receipts against the initial committed spend). We’ll include that language in the draft MSA attached.

2) Marketplace surcharge and invoicing: AWS charges a marketplace fee to sellers that is typically reflected in our seller-side economics, not as a visible surcharge on the buyer invoice line item. For you, the invoice will be from AWS (if you transact via the marketplace). AWS handles taxes on that invoice per your tax settings in AWS. If you prefer Redwood invoicing directly, that’s part of the direct contract path. Both are supported — marketplace for speed, direct for custom billing.

3) Timeline: Private Offer can often be provisioned in 48–72 hours if we have SKU/entitlement details and your procurement completes the acceptance quickly. The typical blocker is procurement sign-off and PO issuance. If you can provide a contact person in procurement and a PO number, we’ll aim for the 3 business day window.

I’ve attached a concise pricing summary showing how credits and discounts would apply across the two routes.

If you’re comfortable, here are two proposed times for a quick sync: Tue 2026-08-04 09:00 PT or Tue 2026-08-04 10:30 PT. Let me know which works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Great — thanks Samantha and Laura. Finalizing recommended next steps below so procurement has an action list:

1) Accept Private Offer: Redwood will create an AWS Marketplace Private Offer for a 3-week POC SKU. We’ll include a line referencing SOC2 evidence (we’ll share the most recent SOC2 report via our secure portal) and data residency notes. We’ll set the offer to be transactable and time-boxed.
2) PO & Procurement contact: Samantha — please share a procurement contact and a PO number or the expected PO timeline so we can provision access immediately after acceptance.
3) Parallel MSA negotiation: Marcus will lead the MSA redlines (he’s copied). We’ll include an explicit credit clause (marketplace spend applied to initial commitment) and any negotiated data controls.
4) Co-sell (optional): If ACME wants AWS engagement, call that out in the meeting and we’ll register the opportunity with AWS Partner Central. Co-sell can help with executive introductions but is not required for the POC.

I’ll send the Private Offer draft and a calendar invite for Tue 10:30 PT pending your confirmation. Thanks again — looking forward to getting you started.
